Implement refresh (single-active-token semantics) and scope-subset requests

approval.cost: No fee for OAuth apps, review, or Figma Community listing is mentioned in the docs read
approval.trigger: Public apps (required for external users) are reviewed by Figma: 'Public OAuth apps can be used to make requests on the behalf of any user that authorizes with your app. When you publish a public OAuth app, Figma reviews it. When Figma approves your public OAuth app, you can then start authorizing users.' The trigger is selecting Public and submitting via Review and submit, with testing instructions (all steps a reviewer needs to test the app; optionally a testing video link; a free trial URL or login credentials for the reviewer if needed) and per-scope reasoning ('you must also provide reasoning for why your app must use each scope'). Private apps need no review: 'Private OAuth apps can be used to make requests on behalf of users in team or organization you associated your app with when you created it. Unlike public OAuth apps, private OAuth apps don't require review by Figma when you publish them.' Pre-approval cap (draft state): 'While in draft, you and admins for your plan can test your OAuth app. The app can't be used to make requests on behalf of other users, including those in your team or organization.' Re-review trap: configuration can be changed after publishing, but 'In the case of published public apps, changes to configuration will require your OAuth app to be re-reviewed.' Existing apps (one-time migration): platform changes 'went into effect on November 17, 2025'; existing OAuth app owners got an 'Update required' label and must re-publish: 'If your OAuth app supports an integration or application for Figma users in general, you'll need to publish your OAuth app as public and get Figma approval.' Listing: an optional Figma Community listing is offered during the publish flow ('List this app on community'); it is separate from the OAuth approval itself.
approval.wait: Not stated (Figma publishes no approval SLA in the docs read)

blockers.detail: 'Authentication codes expire 30 seconds after being issued. You must exchange the code for an access token by calling api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token within 30 seconds of the user completing the OAuth grant.'
blockers.howToClear: Exchange the code synchronously in the callback handler; never queue it.
blockers.title: 30-second code window

blockers.detail: 'Figma only maintains one access token per app for a user, so when you refresh an access token, the previous access token stops working. You'll need to ensure the latest access token is always applied for the user of your app.' Concurrent workers or stale stored tokens break immediately on refresh.
blockers.howToClear: Serialize refreshes per user and always overwrite the stored token atomically.
blockers.title: Single active access token per user per app

blockers.detail: 'This is the only opportunity you have to obtain the Client Secret. The secret is required for token exchange and refreshing access tokens.' No recovery/rotation procedure is described in the pages read.
blockers.howToClear: Store the secret in a secrets manager the moment the app is created.
blockers.title: Client secret is shown once

flavor.recommended: A Public OAuth app using the OAuth 2 authorization code flow, with granular scopes and PKCE (S256)
flavor.why: The object is an OAuth app created at figma.com/developers/apps ('My Apps'). It must be associated with a team or organization ('The OAuth app must be associated with a team or organization'; users of your app do NOT need to belong to it), and exists in one of three states: draft, private, or public. Creation yields a Client ID and Client Secret. 'Currently we only support the authorization code flow for OAuth 2, so the only valid value here is code.' PKCE is 'Optional but highly recommended... Only the S256 method for generating the code challenge is supported.' Figma's guidance: 'Use an OAuth app if your application needs to act on behalf of individual Figma users', and OAuth is the 'Recommended' authentication method (some APIs, Activity Logs and Discovery, require an OAuth app). Scopes are granular and selected at app configuration (the auth request may pass a subset): current_user:read, file_content:read, file_comments:read/write, webhooks:read/write, and more; some are plan-gated (file_variables and library_analytics are Enterprise only; org: scopes need Enterprise, some Governance+, plus an org-admin authorizing user).

humanMust: Create the app in My Apps (name, team or organization) and immediately store the Client Secret (shown once)
Complete the configuration pages: General (private or public), OAuth credentials (redirect URLs), OAuth scopes (with per-scope reasoning), Describe your app (logo and description), Review scopes
For public apps: complete Testing instructions (steps, optional video, free trial URL or reviewer credentials) and submit via Review and submit
name: Figma
nuances: Scope change consequences: 'Your users will only be required to reauthenticate if you add new scopes to your app', and for public apps any configuration change also triggers re-review, so scope selection is effectively frozen once live. Exception: migrating away from the deprecated files:read / file_read scopes to a subset of granular scopes does NOT require reauthentication. Both deprecated scopes 'are being removed under the November 17, 2025 platform changes'.

'Scopes do not supersede the permissions granted to you by an organization or the owner of a folder, team, or file. You can only access files that you've created or that have been shared with you.' The user 'must access the authentication URL using a web browser, not an embedded WebView inside your application. WebView access to the Figma OAuth flow is not supported', and 'If the user rejects the request, no callback is triggered' (handle abandonment without an error redirect).

ID handling: the token response's numeric user_id is deprecated in favor of user_id_string, because many Figma user IDs 'cannot be represented in common number formats such as JavaScript numbers and Go's float64'. OAuth apps can also be reassigned by team/organization admins if the creator leaves.

Figma for Government uses separate endpoints (api.figma-gov.com for token and API). 'The Figma REST API will only allow token exchange with the redirect URLs you specify', so a callback endpoint is a configuration prerequisite.
prerequisites: A Figma team or organization to associate the app with
A callback endpoint (redirect URLs are required configuration)
Testing instructions (and reviewer access, if needed) for the public review

steps.detail: My Apps > Create a new app: enter a name, select a team or organization, Create. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret and store them securely ('This is the only opportunity you have to obtain the Client Secret'). The app is created in draft state.
steps.title: Create the app; capture the secret immediately

steps.detail: General page: name, logo, private or public. OAuth credentials page: Add a redirect URL (one or more). OAuth scopes page: select scopes (with reasoning for each). Describe your app: logo and description. Review scopes: confirm. Private apps: click Publish and you are done (team/organization users only).
steps.title: Configure the app

steps.detail: Testing instructions page: enter all steps a reviewer needs to test the app; optionally add a testing video link; provide a free trial URL or login credentials if needed. Review and submit page: read the summary and app review guidelines, check the submission box, click 'Submit for review'. After approval you may optionally list the app on Figma Community.
steps.title: (Public apps) Submit for Figma review

steps.detail: Direct the user to figma.com/oauth?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&scope=... (a subset of the configured scopes) &state=...&response_type=code, in a real web browser (no embedded WebView). On 'Allow access', Figma redirects to your callback with code and state (verify state). Exchange within 30 seconds: POST api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token with HTTP Basic auth (Base64 of client_id:client_secret), body redirect_uri, code, grant_type=authorization_code (plus code_verifier if PKCE). Response: user_id_string, access_token, expires_in, refresh_token.
steps.title: Run the flow (30-second exchange)

steps.detail: Call the REST API with Authorization: Bearer. Access tokens expire after 90 days by default. Refresh via POST api.figma.com/v1/oauth/refresh with the refresh_token and the same Basic auth; remember only one access token per user is live at a time.
steps.title: Call the API; refresh

tagline: Public OAuth apps need Figma's review before any external user can authorize (private apps skip review but stay inside your own team or org), published-app configuration changes trigger re-review, codes die in 30 seconds, and only one access token per user is ever alive.

time.active: ~20 min of app configuration + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Unknown: review duration is not stated
